What your Google Business Profile does well

Your Business Profile is the listing in the map results: name, phone, hours, reviews, photos, directions. For most local service businesses it's the single most valuable thing online, and it's free. If you haven't claimed and verified yours, do that before anything else.

What a profile can't do on its own

  • It shows your competitors right beside you. The map results put three or more businesses side by side, and Google can show others on and around your listing.
  • It gives Google and AI assistants very little to read. A short description and a category don't explain every service you offer or every town you cover.
  • It can't answer a customer's questions. Do you do this specific job? Do you come to my town? Are you licensed and insured? A profile has little room for that.
  • It's not yours. Google controls the layout, can change features, and can suspend a listing. A page of your own is a stable home your profile, truck and business cards can all point to.

What a simple website adds

You don't need ten pages. You need one page that says what you do, where you do it, and how to reach you, written so Google understands it and a homeowner calls.

  • Every service, in plain words, so you can show up for more searches.
  • Every town you cover, matching your profile's service area.
  • A tap-to-call button and a quote form for people who search after hours.
  • Your name, phone and address exactly as they appear on your profile.
That's exactly what an Enoma page is: one page built from your Google listing, with your services, your towns, tap-to-call and a quote form that sends requests straight to you. See yours in 30 seconds.

How to make them work together

  1. Put your page's link in your Business Profile's website field.
  2. Keep your business name, phone and address identical in both places, down to the suite number.
  3. List the same towns on your page that you list as your service area.
  4. Ask every happy customer for a Google review, and show those reviews on your page.
  5. Use your page's link everywhere else: truck, invoices, Facebook, yard signs.

What about AI assistants like ChatGPT?

More homeowners now ask an AI assistant to recommend a plumber or landscaper. These tools lean on the same signals Google does: a complete profile, consistent business details across the web, reviews, and clear pages that describe what you do and where. A page of your own helps on every one of those.

Common questions

Do I need a website if I have a Google Business Profile?: common questions

Is a Google Business Profile enough without a website?

It's enough to appear on Google Maps, but it gives Google and customers limited information and shows competitors beside you. A simple website with your services, towns and phone number helps you show up for more searches and gives people a place to call you from.

Will a website help my Google Business Profile rank better?

It can. Google uses your website to understand what you do and where. A page that names your services and service towns, with the same name, phone and address as your profile, gives Google more to work with.

What should I put in the website field of my Google Business Profile?

A page you control that matches your profile: your services, the towns you serve, your phone number and a way to request a quote. Avoid linking only to a Facebook page.

Do AI assistants like ChatGPT use my website?

AI assistants draw on public information about your business, including your Google listing, review sites and web pages. Clear, consistent details on a page of your own make it easier for them to understand and describe your business.
